html:
A pledge made by young nationalists at a congress in Batavia on 28 October 1928, declaring one motherland, one nation and one language: Indonesia.

The Dutch East Indies stretched across thousands of islands and hundreds of peoples. Early youth groups were regional, with names like Young Java and Young Sumatra. At the Second Youth Congress their delegates agreed to think of themselves first as Indonesians.

The choice of language mattered most. The delegates picked Malay, long the trade language of the islands' ports, as the basis of Indonesian, rather than Javanese, which more people spoke at home. That choice gave every group an equal footing and spared the country the language fights seen elsewhere. At the same meeting W. R. Supratman played his song "Indonesia Raya" on the violin; it later became the national anthem.

The pledge came a year after Sukarno founded his nationalist party. Seventeen years later Indonesia declared independence. The date is still marked each year as Youth Pledge Day.
sum: A pledge made by young nationalists at a congress in Batavia on 28 October 1928, declaring one motherland, one nation and one language: Indonesia.
